paragraphs: Hyman identifies Issi in the Jerusalem Talmud as Rav Assi, and R' Issi there as Rabbi Assi, or Rabbi Yosi, R' Yonah’s colleague.[^1][^2]

notes.text: These are Hyman’s identifications; Rav Assi, Rabbi Assi and the alternative Rabbi Yosi retain their different title/name forms.

The whole Guggenheimer Avodah Zarah 5:11 paragraph fully names Rabbi Assi and Rabbi Yosi alongside Rabbi Immi. This supplies local title evidence, not proof of Hyman’s general Issi/Assi/Yosi identifications or Yonah-colleague alternative. Uncollated Issi and Yonah use R'; source-fully-written Rav Assi remains Rav. The alternatives and existing note remain without alias or colleague binding.
